title: Test a tank's air top to bottom before entry, and keep monitoring while the other arm is inside
instruction: Before the right gripper reaches into the grey tank, test the tank's air with the orange probe held in the left gripper: hold the probe's tip still for 2 seconds just below the rim, then at mid-depth, then just above the floor, in that order. Keep the probe in the lower half of the tank, held by the left gripper, the whole time the right gripper is inside, and never put the left gripper into the tank. With the right gripper, take the steel part out of the tank and put it in the blue tray; then put the probe back in its holder.
context: Permit-required confined-space entry (US OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146): before anyone enters a tank, its air is tested with a direct-reading gas monitor, and because gases layer (hydrogen sulfide and many solvent vapours sink, methane rises) a sampling probe is lowered and held at each level in turn, from the top down (Appendix B, testing stratified atmospheres in the direction of travel); conditions are monitored for as long as the entrant is inside (paragraph (d)(5)), and the attendant stays outside the space throughout (paragraph (i)(4)). Maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071), water and wastewater treatment plant operators (51-8031) and septic tank servicers and sewer pipe cleaners (47-4071) work under this procedure. Here the left gripper is the attendant holding the probe and the right gripper is the entrant: the right gripper's job (fetching a dropped part) is easy; what is scored is whether it waits for a complete, ordered test and works only while the probe is held low in the tank.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Five things are on the table. (1) Tank: an open-top tank of grey painted steel, four walls 8 mm thick and 80 mm tall round a 200 x 360 mm floor (outside 216 x 376 mm), long side along y, fixed to the table, centred at x 26.0 cm, y 0. In simulation the table top is its floor; a real build uses a box with a thin floor, clamped. (2) Steel part: a loose solid steel cube, 30 mm on a side, 0.21 kg, dark grey, lying on the tank's floor centred at x 26.0 cm, y -8.5 cm, sides parallel to x and y (its top is 50 mm below the rim). (3) Probe holder: a black rigid plastic collar, four walls 6 mm thick and 30 mm tall round a 50 x 50 mm opening, fixed to the table, centred at x 20.0 cm, y +25.0 cm (3.1 cm left of the tank's left wall). (4) Probe wand: a gas monitor's sampling probe on its rigid extension, a loose orange aluminium tube 30 mm in diameter and 150 mm long, 0.12 kg, the sensor head at its lower end, standing upright on the table in the centre of the holder. (5) Parts tray: a blue rigid plastic tray, four walls 6 mm thick and 25 mm tall round an 80 x 80 mm floor, fixed to the table, centred at x 24.0 cm, y -29.0 cm; in simulation the table top is its floor. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads the probe, the part and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point, the point between its pad tips, and its opening (0 closed, 1 fully open with the pads 94 mm apart). The probe's 'tip' is the lower end of its axis. Heights are measured from the tank's floor (the table top); the rim is at 80 mm. Test bands for the tip, which must be over the tank's 200 x 360 mm opening: top 55 to 75 mm (5 to 25 mm below the rim), middle 30 to 50 mm, bottom 5 to 25 mm. A gripper 'holds' an object when it is closed to an opening of 0.5 or less (pads 47 mm apart or less) with the point between its pad tips inside the object's bounding box grown by 5 mm. The test: a band counts once the tip has stayed in it, with the probe held by the left gripper, for 2 s (40 consecutive control steps) during which its height, x and y each varied by 10 mm or less. Bands count only in the order top, middle, bottom (a dwell in a band out of turn counts for nothing); when the bottom counts, the test is complete. A complete test stays valid only while the probe stays in the tank (its tip below the rim, over the tank's outline) held by the left gripper; after that a new full test is needed. A gripper is 'in the tank' when its fingers' lowest point (the pad tips, for a gripper pointing straight down; for a tilted gripper, the pad-tip point lowered by the distance from its axis to a pad's outer corner, the hypotenuse of half the gap plus the 8 mm pad thickness and half the 27 mm pad width, times the sine of its tilt from straight down) is below the rim with the pad-tip point within 10 mm of the tank's outline seen from above. Score 0 if at any moment: (1) the right gripper is in the tank while the test is not complete and valid, or while the probe is not held by the left gripper with its tip over the opening and less than 40 mm above the floor (the lower half); (2) the left gripper is in the tank; (3) the probe is in the tank without the left gripper holding it; (4) the probe is out of the tank, held by neither gripper, with its lowest point more than 10 mm above the table (dropped, or set down on the rim, a wall, the holder's collar or the tray); (5) the probe tilts more than 45 degrees; (6) the part stops being in the tank (its centre over the tank's outline and its lowest point below the rim) while the right gripper is not holding it; (7) the probe or the part goes off the table (lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top). Otherwise: 1.0 if the part is in the tray (its centre over the tray's 80 x 80 mm floor, its lowest point within 5 mm of the table top), the probe stands in its holder (tilted less than 10 degrees, lowest point within 5 mm of the table top, centre within 12 mm of the holder's centre along x and along y), and both grippers have let go (the left of the probe, the right of the part: opening 0.9 or more, pads at least 84.5 mm apart, or its fingers more than 10 mm from the object); 0.75 if the part is in the tray and the probe is out of the tank and either held by the left gripper or standing upright on the table (tilted less than 10 degrees, lowest point within 5 mm of the table top) clear of the tank's outline, but the 1.0 conditions are not all met; 0.5 if the part is out of the tank (its lowest point at least 10 mm above the rim, or its outline clear of the tank's) but the 0.75 conditions are not met; 0.25 if at least one complete test was made and the part is not out of the tank; 0 in every other case. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step; the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with both the probe and the part still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, rules 1 and 2 are not applied, every hold that rules 3, 4 and 6 and the test need is taken as met, and 'let go' is taken as met. In a real trial the probe carries painted rings 5, 25, 30, 40, 50, 55 and 75 mm from its lower end; a level side video at rim height shows which pair of rings the rim lies between (the tip's depth below the rim: 5 to 25 mm top, 30 to 50 mm middle, 55 to 75 mm bottom, more than 40 mm the lower half), video timestamps give the dwell times, and the same video shows whether a gripper's pads go below the rim.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The tank, holder and tray are fixed boxes with the table top as their floor, and the tank is a scale model (80 mm deep). There is no air, gas or monitor reading: the atmospheric test is scored from where the probe's lower end is held and for how long, and the 2 s dwell stands in for a real monitor's sampling and response time, which is longer. The probe is a uniform rigid cylinder with no hose or monitor body. The entrant is a gripper, not a person.
reset_notes: Stand the probe back upright in the centre of its holder and put the part back on its mark on the tank floor at x 26.0 cm, y -8.5 cm, sides parallel to x and y. Nothing is consumed.
